faqs.a: Nope — my planning services are completely free to you. I'm paid by the travel companies (the cruise lines, Disney, Universal, and the resorts), not by my clients. You'll pay the same price as booking it yourself, but you get an expert in your corner.
faqs.q: Do you charge a fee for planning my trip?

faqs.a: Because a great trip has a hundred tiny decisions — which ship, which deck, which stateroom, which park days — and I make them every day. Plus, if anything goes sideways before or during your trip, you call me instead of sitting on hold with a 1-800 number.
faqs.q: Why book with a travel advisor instead of doing it myself?

faqs.a: Cruises, Walt Disney World and Disneyland, Universal Orlando and Hollywood, beach getaways, and Europe. If it's an option on my quote form, I plan it — and if you're dreaming of something else entirely, just ask.
faqs.q: What kinds of trips do you plan?

faqs.a: As early as you can — 6 to 12 months out is the sweet spot for cruises and Disney, when prices and availability are at their best. But if your trip is next month, reach out anyway. I'd rather help late than not at all.
faqs.q: How far in advance should I reach out?

faqs.a: You contact me and I handle it — rebooking, rearranging, and dealing with the travel companies so you don't have to. That's the whole point of having an advisor instead of a confirmation email.
faqs.q: What happens if something goes wrong on my trip?

faqs.a: Fill out the quote form and tell me about your dream trip. I'll send back hand-picked options, we narrow it down together, and I handle all the booking details. You just pack.
